records.submitted_prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Image1 is the ORIGINAL card illustration and the strict EDIT TARGET. The previous pass only swapped characters and looked plain and standard: this pass must feel INVENTIVE, reinterpreting the replaced subject as a specific Persona 3 Reload moment, character or object, while the card stays instantly recognizable at thumbnail size: same silhouettes, same action, same footprint, same camera. Keep the exact background: its palette, large shapes, lighting direction, cast shadows, magical effects, enemies and core objects stay as in Image1 unless this prompt names them. Do NOT redraw the scene, do NOT recolor globally, do NOT move or rescale anything beyond what is stated. Completely remove the replaced Regent parts (old brown/gold four-point hat-head, gold gauntlets, blue robe, armor) with no remnants left behind, and refill the cleared area with the original background shapes. Match the original's rich hard cel-shading: crisp dark outlines, deep near-black occlusion planes, clear midtone and lit planes, material thickness, purposeful small details; no blur, no soft glow, no photoreal rendering. Makoto Yuki's face and head never appear (hands and sleeves only); other characters' faces are allowed. Persona creatures' hands are plump cartoon mittens with no long human fingers. If a named character's design is uncertain, follow the described features, keep the rest simple, and never invent text. Keep important features inside x8-92%, y10-85% (crop-safe). Output: opaque, full-bleed, horizontal 1000x760, no text, letters, numbers, frame, UI or watermark. Never use Pyro Jack, Jack Frost or Pixie in this card. There is no character. Keep the diagonal sword, the gold slash fragments, the sparkles and the purple-magenta background. The sword becomes MAKOTO SWORD bursting OUT of a SWORDS CARD: the card sits at the hilt end (upper left), tilted, its lower half shattering into pale-blue glass shards as the blade springs out of it along the original diagonal. Same sword length, angle and position. Character and object designs: [MAKOTO SWORD] = Makoto's sword: plain silver straight single-edge blade, simple silver crossguard, black wrapped grip, round silver pommel. [SWORDS CARD] = a Shuffle Time minor-arcana SWORDS card: a royal-blue and gold tarot card showing a single upright sword emblem, no text or numerals.
Image2 is the sword design reference ONLY. Use its silver straight blade, crossguard, black wrapped grip and round pommel, not its green background or horizontal placement. Image1 remains the sole edit target.

records.name: strike_regent
records.submitted_prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Image1 is the current candidate and the edit target. Fix ONE problem: the sword looks bent because its grip and pommel are angled flatter (about 18 degrees) than the blade (about 35 degrees), with a kink at the crossguard. Make the whole sword ONE perfectly straight rigid object: pommel, grip, crossguard center, blade spine and tip all on a single straight axis. Keep the blade exactly where it is (same angle, length and tip position at the lower right); redraw only the grip and pommel so they continue the blade's axis up and to the left (the pommel ends at about x27%, y33% of the canvas), with the crossguard exactly perpendicular to that axis. Move the Swords tarot card along with the pommel so the sword still bursts out of the card at the hilt end, keeping the card's design, its tilt relative to the sword, and the pale-blue glass shards around the breaking point. Keep the gold slash fragments, the sparkles, the warm glow and the purple-magenta background unchanged. Crisp hard cel-shading. Opaque, full-bleed, same size as Image1, no text, frame or watermark.

straightness_check.method: Visual straight-line overlay on 1000x760 export; manually located pommel center and blade tip
straightness_check.result: Grip centerline, crossguard center and blade spine visually follow the same axis with no obvious original kink; approximate visual check, not a pixel-exact geometry guarantee
